data:
The International Association for Collective Dynamics (IACD) is a non-profit scientific association registered in Germany. Its seat is in Düren. It is entered in the Vereinsregister of the Amtsgericht Düren under VR 3143 (29 July 2026).
The IACD provides an organisational framework for researchers, practitioners and students working in collective dynamics. This includes pedestrian and evacuation dynamics, crowd science, traffic and granular flow, and related fields. The association supports the continuity of the conferences PED (Pedestrian and Evacuation Dynamics) and TGF (Traffic and Granular Flow), and aims to strengthen the wider research community.

data.documents#Documents: The statutes are available in German and English. The German version is authoritative (§13). The statutes, admission guidelines and code of conduct are on the Documents page.
data.founding-members#Founding members: The IACD was founded by 24 members on 18 June 2026, during the steering committee meeting at TGF26 in Bristol.
data.governance#Governance:
The IACD has three bodies: the General Assembly (all members), the Executive Board, and the Steering Committee, which serves as a scientific advisory body.
See Board & Auditors and the FAQ for details.
data.purpose#Purpose:
Research in collective dynamics spans disciplines and countries. The IACD provides a place for people working in these fields to meet, exchange ideas and support shared activities.
Under §2 of its statutes, the IACD promotes science and research, as well as civic and professional education, in the field of collective dynamics. Its activities include organising and supporting scientific conferences, promoting international cooperation and good scientific practice, publishing scientific results, and supporting young researchers.
The association acts selflessly and pursues exclusively non-profit purposes.

data.are-there-membership-fees#Are there memb:
Fees are set by the General Assembly in a fee schedule (§4a). The schedule adopted on 2 November 2026 is:
Category 1 year 2 years 3 years Regular €50 €90 €130 Student & early-career €10 €15 €20 Membership runs by calendar year. The first membership year is 2027: you can join and pay at any time, and membership starts on 1 January 2027. From 2027, joining from 1 July costs half the 1-year fee for the rest of that year. Paying 2 or 3 years upfront gets a discount. Members may receive a discount on PED/TGF registration — none at PED27, and a discount of up to ~5% from TGF28 onward, agreed per conference. The board may also reduce or waive fees on justified request (§4a).
data.can-i-promote-iacd-and-recruit-members-o: Yes — every member is an ambassador. You may promote IACD, share announcements, and invite colleagues to join. One distinction: official representation (binding statements or commitments in the association’s name) is legally reserved to the Executive Board (two board members jointly, §6(3)). For official text or commitments, coordinate with the board; informal advocacy is open to everyone.
data.how-do-i-join#How do I join?: Membership applications are made in writing (including electronically) to the Executive Board, which decides on admission (§4(3)). To apply, email board [at] collectivedynamics.org with your name, affiliation, membership category and term; see How to join.
data.how-is-the-steering-committee-chosen#How: The General Assembly (all voting members) elects or confirms the Steering Committee — not the board alone (§7(5), §11(2)). Nominations may come from members or from the board; the General Assembly then votes (simple majority). It may include both association members and external experts; board members may also serve (§11(2)). Size: 5–30 members. Term: 2 years, reappointment allowed (§11(3), Admission Guidelines). Composition reflects geographic, disciplinary, and gender diversity; members should generally have taken part in PED or TGF (§11(2)).
data.i-attended-the-founding-meeting-and-sign: No. You are already a founding member — you do not re-apply. Once the membership system is live, you will simply complete a short online profile (and pay dues once a fee schedule is set), so the board has a clean member register. This is a formality for record-keeping, not a second admission.
data.what-bodies-does-iacd-have#What bodies d: General Assembly — all members; highest decision-making body. Executive Board — Chair, Deputy Chair, Treasurer; runs day-to-day business. Steering Committee — scientific advisory body for PED and TGF. Authoritative rules are in the Statutes (German version prevails, §13) and the Admission Guidelines. This FAQ is for information only. Contact and website details will follow.
data.what-does-the-steering-committee-do#What:
It provides strategic and scientific guidance for the PED and TGF conferences —
selection of organizing teams, scientific direction, and the composition of
scientific committees (§11(4)). The Executive Board decides on conference hosting
rights based on its recommendations.
data.what-is-expected-of-me-as-a-member#What: Support the association’s aims, follow the Code of Conduct, and pay dues once set. Holding an office is not required. Members are warmly encouraged to help the community grow — invite colleagues and spread the word.
data.what-types-of-membership-are-there#What:
Membership is for individuals (institutional or company memberships are not offered). The association distinguishes members with and without voting rights. Unless the Executive Board decides otherwise at admission, new members are voting members by default.
Voting members — paying members with full rights. They may:
take part in the General Assembly, vote, stand for election to the Executive Board and other elected bodies, receive all member benefits. Reduced-fee members (students and early-career researchers) — a reduced rate applies (see fees), kept as voting members with the same rights.
Non-voting members — admitted by the Executive Board where participation is mainly for scientific exchange, advisory involvement, or support, without taking part in formal governance. They do not vote or stand for office. The board decides whether they pay a fee.
In short: most members are voting members; a reduced rate may be added later; and non-voting is a special category for advisory/supporting roles.
data.who-can-become-a-member#Who can become a:
Any individual who supports the aims of the association (Statutes §4(1)).
Researchers, practitioners, and students across all regions and disciplines are
welcome — international participation is intended by design.

data: Membership is open. See How to join below. Membership is open to anyone who supports the aims of the association: researchers, practitioners, and students across all regions and disciplines. International participation is intended by design.
data.benefits-of-membership#Benefits of membe:
Membership is, above all, a way to belong to and support the community. Being a member is intended to offer the following.
From the start Awards. Best paper and best poster awards at each PED and TGF, open to members. A winner who is not yet a member receives a complimentary 3-year membership. PhD workshops and training. Reduced fees and priority registration for members at PhD workshops and training courses held alongside PED and TGF, such as the PED25 PhD workshop. Discounts on future conferences. We aim to secure a member discount on PED/TGF registration. There will be none at PED27 (its budget is already fixed), but up to ~5% from TGF28 onward, agreed with each conference’s organizers and announced per event. A voice in the community. Members vote in the General Assembly, can nominate and be elected to the Steering Committee, and get priority for roles such as reviewing and programme committees. Online seminars. A regular seminar series where members, especially PhD students, present their work to the community. Jobs and calls. Members can share PhD, postdoc, and industry positions, datasets, and calls through the association’s channels. A wider network. Membership connects you with researchers and practitioners across regions and disciplines working on pedestrian and traffic dynamics. Planned as the association grows Best PhD thesis award. IACD Fellows. Recognition of members with outstanding contributions to the field. Mentoring. Senior members paired with PhD members, for example around the PhD workshops. Special interest groups, e.g. experiments and data, modelling and software, traffic and granular flow, and crowd safety practice, organising sessions at PED and TGF. Regional groups (e.g. China, Japan, Europe) for members who cannot easily travel to the conferences. Travel grants for PhD members, especially from lower-income countries. Support for colleagues in need. In urgent situations, the association may help members who cannot afford conference or membership fees. This is discretionary and exceptional, not a guaranteed entitlement: the board may reduce or waive fees on justified request (Statutes §4a). A closer link with the community’s journal, the open-access Collective Dynamics, e.g. through member reviewers and editors.
data.fees#Fees:
Adopted by the General Assembly on 2 November 2026.
Category 1 year 2 years 3 years Regular €50 €90 €130 Student & early-career €10 €15 €20 All members are full voting members. Membership runs by calendar year (1 January to 31 December). The first membership year is 2027: you can join and pay at any time, and your membership starts on 1 January 2027. From 2027, if you join between 1 July and 31 December, you pay half the 1-year fee for the rest of that year, then renew in January. Paying 2 or 3 years upfront gets a discount. Paying upfront also helps build the reserves that let IACD support the conferences directly. For students and early-career members, 3 years covers a typical PhD.
data.how-to-join#How to join:
Membership is a way to support the community, not a conference fee. The benefits above are secondary.
To join, write to board [at] collectivedynamics.org with your name, affiliation, membership category (regular, or student and early-career) and term (1, 2 or 3 years). Once the board has accepted your application, we will send you the payment details:
From Europe (SEPA area): please pay by bank transfer, which is free of charge for you and for the association. From outside Europe: pay online with a secure payment link (Stripe), which avoids high international transfer fees.
data.membership-types#Membership types: Voting members — the default. Full rights: take part in the General Assembly, vote, stand for election, and receive all member benefits. Students & early-career researchers — a reduced rate (see fees). They are voting members with the same rights. Non-voting members — admitted by the Executive Board for advisory or supporting roles, without taking part in formal governance.
data.questions#Questions?: See the FAQ for details on voting rights, the Steering Committee, and how the association is run, or email board [at] collectivedynamics.org.
data.who-can-join#Who can join: Any individual who supports the association’s aims (Statutes §4). Membership is for individuals. There is no corporate or institutional membership.

data:
Press release from the PTED 2026 organisers.
From November 13 to 15, 2026, the 7th Workshop on Pedestrian Traffic and Evacuation Dynamics (PTED 2026) was held in Hefei, Anhui Province, China. It was organized by the State Key Laboratory of Fire Science at the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), and co-organized by the Joint National–Local Engineering Research Centre for Hot Safety Technology and the Personnel Safety Professional Committee of the China Association for Public Safety Science and Technology. The chairs of the workshop are Prof. Weiguo Song and Prof. Jun Zhang from USTC.
The workshop serves as a forum for exchanging new theories, methods, technologies and trends in pedestrian and evacuation dynamics research and for jointly exploring the field’s future directions. It attracted over 140 scholars from 33 institutions, including the National University of Defense Technology, Southwest Jiaotong University, Central South University, the University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, Wuhan University of Technology, Qingdao University of Technology, Sichuan University, Beijing University of Technology, Hefei University of Technology, Southeast University, Jiangsu University, Fujian Police College, City University of Hong Kong and the host institution, USTC.
Prof. Xin Lv from the National University of Defense Technology, Dr. Maik Boltes from Forschungszentrum Jülich, and Prof. Wei Lv from Wuhan University of Technology delivered keynote lectures. Focusing on frontier issues — including data science approaches for emergency management in the intelligent era, experimental data collection methods in pedestrian dynamics, and wargaming methods for emergency evacuation — the three experts presented a systematic overview of the latest research advances in the field, analysed the research trajectory of data collection, governance and modelling, and offered their perspectives on the field’s future development directions.
Prof. Eric Lee from City University of Hong Kong, Prof. Xiaoxia Yang from Qingdao University of Technology, Dr. Zhigang Shi from the University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, Associate Prof. Zhijian Fu from Southwest Jiaotong University, and Associate Prof. Yunhe Tong from Central South University delivered invited thematic talks in turn. Twenty-four scholars and experts from Beijing Jiaotong University, Sun Yat-sen University, the University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, China University of Petroleum (Beijing), Wuhan University of Technology and other universities gave excellent oral presentations. Participants held in-depth exchanges and discussions on topics such as pedestrian traffic, emergency evacuation, psychology and decision-making, virtual reality technology and artificial intelligence technology, sharing their research results, experience and views, and actively exploring new research directions and solutions. The open and interactive atmosphere provided valuable opportunities for learning and exchange, fostering the cross-fertilization of ideas and academic progress across research directions.
data.iacd-at-pted-2026#IACD at PTED 2026: Workshop chair Prof. Jun Zhang, Deputy Chair of the IACD, presented the association to the participants and invited them to join. This made the IACD known in the Chinese research community and strengthens its international character.

data:
The 16th Traffic and Granular Flow conference (TGF26) took place from 16 to 19 June 2026 at the University of Bristol, UK. The programme had five keynote lectures, more than 60 talks and close to 50 posters.
On 18 June, the TGF steering committee extended its meeting into the founding meeting of the International Association for Collective Dynamics. 24 members founded the association, adopted its statutes and elected the first Executive Board: Andreas Schadschneider (Chair), Jun Zhang (Deputy Chair) and Mohcine Chraibi (Treasurer). The IACD was entered in the Vereinsregister of the Amtsgericht Düren on 29 July 2026.
The next TGF will be held in Wuppertal, Germany, from 6 to 9 June 2028, under the umbrella of the IACD. See TGF28.
Nikolai Bode has written a full report on the conference, with the keynotes and the social programme, on pedestriandynamics.org.

data.7-your-rights#7. Your rights:
You have the right to access (Art. 15 GDPR), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction of processing (Art. 18), data portability (Art. 20) and to object to processing based on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (Art. 21). To exercise these rights, write to us at the address above.
You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority. The authority responsible for us is the Landesbeauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit Nordrhein-Westfalen (LDI NRW), Kavalleriestraße 2–4, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany.

data.about-the-series#About the series:
Traffic and Granular Flow brings together researchers studying the dynamics of interacting many-particle systems — vehicular and pedestrian traffic, granular materials, and related collective phenomena — across physics, engineering, mathematics, and the social sciences. TGF28 is organised under the umbrella of the IACD, which provides the conference’s long-term organisational continuity.
More details — programme, registration, and key dates — will follow. To stay informed, watch collective-dynamics.eu or write to board [at] collectivedynamics.org.
